alerts.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 28 at 3:48AM HST until September 28 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR SOUTH FACING SHORES OF ALL
HAWAIIAN ISLANDS...

...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR WEST FACING SHORES OF THE BIG
ISLAND...

.Rough short to medium period south-southwest swell from
Hurricane Nolo is expected to generate a quick pulse of advisory
level surf for south facing shores of all islands and west facing
shores of the Big Island today. While this is currently forecast
to gradually fade below advisory thresholds tonight, there is some
uncertainty in how quickly this will occur and it is possible
that advisory level surf may persist through Tuesday even as the
swell becomes southwesterly.

* WHAT...For south facing shores, large surf becoming 7 to 10 ft
today. For west facing shores of the Big Island, large surf
becoming 6 to 8 ft today.

* WHERE...West facing shores of the Big Island and south facing
shores of all Hawaiian Islands (excluding Southeast Big Island).

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.
alerts.instruction:
Heed all advice from ocean safety officials. When in doubt, don't
go out.

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM HST Mon Sep 28 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located near Baja California Sur, on Hurricane Nolo, located
several hundred miles southwest of the main Hawaiian Islands, and
on Tropical Storm Rachel, located a couple of hundred miles
south-southwest of Acapulco, Mexico.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (EP91):
Showers and thunderstorms are limited and disorganized in
association with an area of low pressure located well east-southeast
of the Hawaiian Islands. Although the system has lost some
organization today, it is still expected to become a tropical
depression during the next day or two while it drifts northeastward.
Environmental conditions are expected to become less conducive for
development late this week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

aiBriefing: Obecnie na Hawajach jest podwyższony poziom zagrożenia (2/5), głównie z powodu bliskości huraganu Nolo (kategoria 4, ok. 674 km od trasy) oraz wysokiego (90%) prawdopodobieństwa uformowania się nowego systemu tropikalnego w ciągu tygodnia. Ostrzeżenie o wysokim przyboju (High Surf Advisory) obowiązywało tylko do 28 września do 18:00 czasu hawajskiego, czyli zakończyło się zanim zaczniecie podróż 2 października — nie powinno mieć na Was bezpośredniego wpływu. Sam Nolo, mimo silnej kategorii, znajduje się setki kilometrów od Waszej trasy i to on odpowiada za wspomniany przybój, który już opadł. Warto natomiast na bieżąco śledzić rozwój nowego, nienazwanego jeszcze systemu (EP91), bo jego dalszy rozwój i tor są jeszcze niepewne, a wasza podróż zaczyna się już za 3 dni. Poza tym nic w danych nie wskazuje na bezpośrednie zagrożenie dla Oahu, Big Island czy Maui w terminach Waszej podróży.
